conventions.convention: A right coaction has type ρ:M→M⊗C. Comodule maps satisfy ρ_N f=(f⊗id_C)ρ_M. Subcomodules are injective comodule maps, identified with images after constructing the image coaction.
C* is the full algebraic dual. Convolution is (f*g)(c)=(f⊗g)Δ(c), with f on the first factor, g on the second, and unit ε. Right comodules induce left C*-modules.
Rationality requires, for each m, one finite tensor t_m whose evaluations represent f·m for every f∈C*. Uniqueness is a proved consequence under the correspondence theorem's hypotheses.
The full arbitrary-coalgebra correspondence assumes AC; the forward construction is choice-free, and the full correspondence for finite-dimensional C is choice-free.

Coefficient indices are fixed by ρ(v_j)=Σ_i v_i⊗c_ij, giving Δ(c_ij)=Σ_ℓ c_iℓ⊗c_ℓj and ε(c_ij)=δ_ij. The coefficient characterization is independent of the AC assumption used for arbitrary-dimensional kernels and quotients.

Full-dual algebra-to-coalgebra transposition requires the algebra itself to be finite-dimensional. The tensor-dual pairing preserves factor order, and the finite bidual identifications are evaluation maps.

load_bearing.statement: A right C-comodule is a k-vector space M with a linear map ρ_M:M→M⊗C satisfying (ρ_M⊗id_C)ρ_M=(id_M⊗Δ)ρ_M and (id_M⊗ε)ρ_M=id_M. A comodule map f satisfies ρ_N f=(f⊗id_C)ρ_M.

For a finite-dimensional unital associative k-algebra A, A* is a coalgebra under the transpose of multiplication and unit. For every coalgebra C, C* is a unital associative convolution algebra. Dualization reverses structure maps, and on finite-dimensional objects the two contravariant dualizations are inverse equivalences via canonical evaluation.

Assume AC and let C be a coalgebra over a field k. Evaluation of a right coaction identifies right C-comodules and their maps with rational left C*-modules and their maps; the representing tensor is unique. If C is finite-dimensional every left C*-module is rational and the full correspondence is choice-free. The forward construction is choice-free for every C.

The regular pair (C,Δ) is a right comodule. Under AC, kernels and images of comodule maps and M/ker(f) inherit coactions, and M/ker(f)→im(f) is a comodule isomorphism. For ρ(v_j)=Σ_i v_i⊗c_ij, the identities Δ(c_ij)=Σ_ℓ c_iℓ⊗c_ℓj and ε(c_ij)=δ_ij hold; conversely those identities define a right coaction by that formula.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 says: “Applying $\operatorname{id}_M\otimes\varepsilon$ to $\rho_M(v_j)=v_j$ and then applying $\lambda_r$ gives …”. The displayed equality ρ_M(v_j)=v_j is ill-typed: its sides belong to M⊗C and M. The intended argument is the counit equation (id_M⊗ε)ρ_M(v_j)=v_j, followed by λ_r. This is a wording error; the coefficient conclusion is correct.

The finite-dimensional dual Hopf theorem cites finite algebra-coalgebra duality in F2 with the correct finite-object restriction and pairing order. Its proof does not infer a full-dual coalgebra for an arbitrary infinite-dimensional algebra.
